question: As of October 15, 2026, will TEPCO report that the Unit 2 robotic arm operation at Fukushima Daiichi is suspended due to a problem?

calls.reasoning: Status quo as of Oct 5: arm insertion began Oct 2 with no major troubles; no reports found of any problem since. YES requires a problem-related suspension in effect on Oct 15 JST, a point-in-time state with ~10 days left. Reference: the 2024 telescopic-device campaign had two problem suspensions (pipe-order error, camera failure) over ~2 months, and this arm had a rusted joint motor in summer 2026, so fault hazard is real; but the 2025 campaign ran smoothly, and short glitches may be fixed before Oct 15. Hazard of roughly 25-35% per month of a problem stoppage, times the chance it is still in effect and reported on Oct 15, gives about 8%. No prediction market found (Polymarket/Manifold none per harness; no Kalshi/bookmaker market found).
calls.dossier:
- Oct 2 2026 (Japan Times, Tokyo Shimbun, FTV): TEPCO opened the X-6 isolation valve at 10:00 JST and advanced the ~22 m, 4.6 t arm tip ~1.2 m into the PCV, washing sediment with a water jet. Work ended 13:07 with 'no major troubles'. Plan: 3-4 months cutting rails/cables and gathering 3D data, then trial debris retrieval in early 2027; ~6 months total.
- Jul 30 2026 (Kyodo via webun/Hokkaido Shimbun/Ryukyu Shimpo): during July checks the 3rd of 7 arm joints could not bend; its motor was to be replaced.
- Sep 15 2026 (Fukushima Central TV/Yahoo; Kyodo): cause was rust inside the motor, likely from water ingress during a March 2026 waterproof test. Motor replaced and operation normal; added waterproofing measures planned.
- History: the arm was delayed 4 times from its 2021 target (COVID, accuracy, Sept 2025 slip to FY2026).
- 2024 telescopic-device campaign (AP/Fox, NEI): Aug 22 halted by human error (push pipes in wrong order); Sep 17 halted when 2 cameras failed (radiation suspected); restarted late Oct after camera swap. That is two problem halts in ~2 months. The 2025 second telescopic campaign was reported as resumed and run without major halts (NEI).
- Searched and found no reports dated Oct 3-5 2026 of any arm problem or suspension. TEPCO English news-release page returned HTTP 403, so it was not checked directly.
- Status quo: work proceeding intermittently with routine daily valve open/close.
- Resolution: resolves off TEPCO releases or credible press reporting a problem-caused halt IN EFFECT on Oct 15 JST. Routine daily stops, weekends and planned steps do not count.
- Event window: reporting up to Oct 15 2026, state as of Oct 15 JST; operation began Oct 2. As of Oct 5 02:30 UTC, ~3 of ~13 days since start have elapsed (~23%), with ~10.5 days left.
- Markets: none found.
calls.reference_class: Fukushima Daiichi Unit 2 remote-device PCV campaigns 2024-2026 (telescopic device x2, robotic arm commissioning): problem-caused halts per ~10-day window

calls.reasoning: Status quo as of Oct 5, 2026 (day 3 of a ~6-month campaign): no reported problem after the Oct 2 insertion. Japanese local TV (FTV, Chukyo TV, TUF) and Japan Times all describe work going to plan. The reference class is past Unit 2 trial-retrieval campaigns with remote devices. In the 2024 telescopic-device campaign there were 2 problem-related suspensions in about 2.5 months: the pipe-order error in Aug 2024 and the camera failure in Sep 2024, which caused a stop of several weeks. The 2025 second retrieval had fewer. This arm also has its own record of faults, including the joint brake rust and the arm failing to extend in July 2026. Reasons it could go YES: a new device, early in the campaign, with a history of faults, and fault stops have tended to last weeks, so one starting before Oct 15 would likely still be in effect. Reasons for NO: only about 10 days remain, the work so far is slow and limited (water-jet cleaning near the entry), and the problem would have to be reported and still be in effect on Oct 15 JST. Market check: I found no market on Polymarket, Manifold or Kalshi, and no bookmaker line.

calls.reasoning: Status quo: the arm went in on Oct 2, 2026, and the first day was reported as having no major trouble. No reports of a fault or halt were found through Oct 5. The reference class is remote-device campaigns at Unit 2. The 2024 Telesco campaign had two problem halts in its first ~2.5 months, one of them on day one. The 2025 campaign had none of note. This arm's own record (rusted joint motor in July 2026, camera swaps) points to a higher hazard. Even so, YES needs a problem-caused halt that is reported and still in effect on Oct 15 JST, and only ~10 days remain. Work is slow and early-stage. Fault stops at 1F usually last weeks, so if a fault happens it would likely still be in effect on Oct 15. Roughly 18-22% chance of a fault in the window times ~55% persistence and reporting gives ~10%. No human market found.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the facts: insertion on Oct 2 with no major trouble, no reported problem through Oct 5, the joint-motor rust fault in July-Sept 2026, two problem halts in the 2024 Telesco campaign and none of note in 2025, and no market. No factual dispute needed settling, and none could be checked here because this run had no web access. The spread (0.08-0.13) is pure judgment about two things: how likely a fault is in the window, and how likely it is to still be in effect on Oct 15. Run 3's point holds that 1F fault stops have lasted weeks (the Sept 2024 camera stop lasted ~5 weeks), so persistence is fairly high. Against that, the early work is low-intensity (water-jet cleaning near the entry), which argues for a lower near-term fault rate than the Telesco day-one error suggests. I'd bet on ~10%.
